newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MAY 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MAY 29.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI
--Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, is flying on automatic pilot with flight scheduling problems increasing conflicts beteeen cabin crews and other unions and the administration increase.
--Government and industrialists spoke the same language on the problems facing the economy and how best to deal with them at yesterday's general assembly of the Federation of Greek Industries (SEV).
--National Mortgage Bank will offer cheaper housing loans as of next week, according to reports. Refinancing of older debts and the presentation of new lending products are also on the cards.
--Charter flight bookings are down over last year's figures, according to latest figures, but hotel stays in April were up slightly.
IMERISIA
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis urged industrialists yesterday to make more investments and take advantage of high business profits appearing over the last few years.

--There will be new guidelines placed on the shares of non-listed companies on the Athens Stock Exchange. Deputy Finance Minister George Drys said the movement of these shares will be made with contractural or private agreements certified by tax officials.
KERDOS
--The terrorist group November 17 is thought to be behind the murder yesterday of shipowner Costas Peratikos.
--Greek industry has increased its profits dramatically over the past few years, according to figures presented at yesterday's SEV general assembly.
--The Bank of Greece has organised a meeting tomorrow with experts from Europe to discuss unemployment in Europe, on the initiative of governor Lucas Papademos.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Although the government is promising bold steps, SEV says that Greek industry has lost ground over the past decade in terms of competitiveness. The sector would be at better levels if the reform of the wider public sector had gone ahead.
--The St George Mills will purchase pasta makers Stella. Stella saw sales of 5,120 million drachmas last year and profits of 36 million drachmas.
EXPRESS
--The Bank of Greece was once again effective at protecting the drachma at yesterday's fixing session, demonstrating once again that exchange policy is and remains anti-inflationary.
--The head of the economic crimes squad SDOE yesterday warned merchants and businessmen to beware bogus tax officials offering to "handle" tax affairs and extorting money.

--The European Commission is to investigate charges that Greece has not maintained Community directives regarding 140 old shares from the Bank of Central Greece. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
